buckets.name: Agent tools
buckets.title: Sun times, space, satellite and biodiversity lookups an agent can call
buckets.build: Wrap one sun-times URL as a get_sun_times tool: pass a latitude and longitude, return sunrise, sunset and day length; add space-weather and GBIF lookups as separate tools with a timeout.
buckets.filter_text: tags has agent-ready AND subcategory matches /^Sun times|satellite/space|GBIF/i

notes.text: are sunrise and sunset queries for one city each; change lat and lng (or lon) in the URL for any other place.

recommended.criteria: Services in this pack with the most endpoints that match this bucket and are tagged `agent-ready` (no key sent in the test call, JSON body, passed a data call). Ties go to the service with more country codes, then by name. Only services with at least one bucket row that matches the focus rule are listed, and the sample comes from those rows; the counts cover the whole bucket. The sample URL is the first row by URL sort after preferring, in this order: rows that match the bucket's sample preference when it has one, rows that return values rather than describe a dataset or a service (not ERDDAP /info/ pages, OGC GetCapabilities requests, bare OWS addresses, PxWeb tables, UN SDG series lists, Statistics Canada download pointers, WorldPop listings, GTFS validation reports, untitled rows or service root addresses), and agent-ready rows. Sample preference in this bucket: `url matches /sunrise-sunset\.org/json\?lat=|/sunrise/3\.0/sun\?lat=|publishingCountry=|planetary-k-index|gp\.php\?GROUP=|events\?status=|launches/upcoming|satellites/\?format=/i`. Services named "ArcGIS organization" hold map layers from many owners and are added only when fewer than 5 other services match.

limits.text: 28.5% of rows carry country code IN; 41,671 rows have no code (global or unknown).
25 rows come from PxWeb or Statistics Canada services. Some statistics endpoints return metadata or a pointer on GET; the table may need a second request or a POST.
4,179 rows are map-layer queries with resultRecordCount set: the tested call asked for a few records; change the query to get the full layer.
195 rows carry limit=1: the tested call asked for one record; raise the limit or page through.
1 rows are open-data portal dataset records, which may return a dataset record with links rather than the table itself.
241 rows are files (zip 146, txt 95) rather than bodies an agent reads directly.

3 rows are service root addresses (the host alone or an API or version path such as /v1, with no query), which may describe the service rather than return data; the sample, examples and recommended lists use other rows first.
3,463 rows are layers on ArcGIS Online, where anyone can publish: some are class projects, tests or copies. Check the owner and the fields before you rely on one.

5,220 rows come from one service, the Flemish subsurface service (dov.vlaanderen.be): geological model layers as WFS requests for one feature (`count=1`) or KML exports. Raise `count` for more features.
2,749 rows are sunrise and sunset queries for one city each, from api.sunrise-sunset.org and api.met.no; the tested URLs carry no date, so add one for a given day.
283,909 rows sit in the science category but have no science term in the title or subcategory. Check the title before you use one; they are not used as starting points.
850 rows are about WiFi, internet use, digital services, telecoms, town planning, buildings, food, shops, study programmes or residence permits for study rather than science.

135 rows carry the subcategory label "astronom" or "genom" (cut from words such as gastronomy) but are about restaurants, breweries, regional food products, milk production or packaging. They are not used as starting points.
43 rows are map layers whose subcategory names schools, libraries, substations or pipelines; check the title before you use one. They are not used as starting points.
42 rows from Canadian hosts (.ca) carry country code US or GB in this snapshot; filter by host when you need Canada only.
Stations and feeds can go quiet after their test date; re-test a URL before you rely on it.
Not in this pack: endpoints that need a key or a POST, and URLs that did not pass.
Left out: 478 rows with a private or local address.
Left out: 15 rows with an email-like address.
Left out: 257 ArcGIS Survey123 layers (they can hold people's form answers).
Left out: 15 ArcGIS proxy layers (utility.arcgis.com/usrsvcs and portal /sharing/servers/ addresses) that can call a service with a stored login.
Left out: 4 layers marked editable in the title (they can hold entries that people added).
Left out: 34 ArcGIS layers that keep a form's default service name (they can hold people's form answers).
Left out: 86 rows that passed a data call only from a network location in India.

Left out: 45 ArcGIS class or coursework layers (lab, assignment, exam, quiz, lesson, exercise, tutorial and final-project layers, copies of class layers, layers named for a person or a person's home, and layers whose name ends in a person's name or holds a student number).
Left out: 2 ArcGIS layers that hold reports, comments, submissions or form responses sent in by the public.
Left out: 6 ArcGIS layers that are records about named people (employee, patient, client or donor lists, home addresses, voter lists, sex offender and missing person layers).
Left out: 8 rows of ArcGIS Online organisations that are class accounts (25 layers or more, at least 50% of them class or coursework layers): their other layers are students' work too.

Left out: 193 rows of ArcGIS Online organisations that are class accounts (3 class sets or more in at least 20% of their rows, 10 class sets or more with no organisation name, or layers signed by students read by hand): their other layers are students' work too.
Left out: 21 rows of class sets: one map layer saved under 5 or more students' initials or names in one ArcGIS Online organisation, or in 4 or more students' own organisations.
Left out: 924 rows of the ArcGIS Online organisations of universities, colleges and schools (many of their layers are students' work).
Left out: 2 rows that repeat an address already in the pack.
